title: A Manifold-Aware Topic Modeling Approach via Rank-Based Prototypes
task: Topic discovery with exactly K topics anchored to real corpus documents
problem: Neural topic models produce latent representations not grounded in texts, while clustering pipelines rely on absolute distances distorted by hubness and anisotropy in high-dimensional embedding spaces.
architecture: MARETopic: SBERT document embeddings are projected with UMAP; ranked nearest-neighbour lists encode ordinal neighbourhood structure; a greedy algorithm selects exactly K exemplar documents whose neighbourhoods cover the corpus, scored either by a query-performance predictor plus rank correlation (Corr variant) or by a rank-based diffusion matrix (Diff variant); topic words via c-TF-IDF followed by an inter-topic Maximal Marginal Relevance step.
key_results: 20NG, K = 50: C_V 0.6818, Purity 0.6227, NMI 0.5419 (Corr variant) vs 0.6649, 0.5812, 0.5265 for Top2Vec.
NYT: Purity 0.7084 vs 0.6583 for FASTopic (+5.0 pp); every generative neural model has non-positive NPMI on at least two corpora.
strengths: Training-free (no gradient updates) and each topic is anchored to an inspectable real document.
Rank-based neighbourhoods are robust to hubness and anisotropy of embedding spaces.
Inter-topic MMR raises diversity above BERTopic (0.85-0.88 vs 0.77-0.80).

limitations.text: Evaluated on three English corpora of moderate size (9K-19K documents); very large corpora would need an approximate index.
Topic diversity remains below generative models such as FASTopic.
On Web of Science, Top2Vec reaches higher Purity and NMI; no downstream or intrusion-based evaluation.

notes: Three runs, K = 50 (K = 100 in appendix); CPU-only runtime comparison.
